card.title: Co-Sign This
card.instruction: Get someone to help by making them an official participant who shares responsibility for the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made you co-organizer of Saturday's school trip. Can you approve the bus route?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only volunteered to drive. Your route misses the museum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good catch. Correct it and initial it; then we both own the plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll fix it, but you explain any delays to the parents.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together. I'll introduce you as our transport lead and take the questions beside you.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 co-organizer title, A3 initialed plan and A5 transport-lead introduction make B an official accountable participant.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 route error prompts A3 signed correction; B4 refusal of parent questions prompts A5 shared public role.

relationship.evidence: B2 distinguishes driving from organizing and B4 offers repair with a responsibility boundary.

heightening.evidence: B4 draws a line at explaining delays; A5 makes public explanation part of the newly formalized role.
